sources.title: aquifer a
sources.text: Rain falling on permeable land seeps through soil and rock to replenish an underground aquifer. Paved surfaces reduce this recharge by directing water into drains.

sources.title: aquifer b
sources.text: City drainage engineers enlarged storm sewers to carry runoff away from roads. Their design emphasized preventing street flooding during intense storms.

sources.title: replication a
sources.text: A replicated database keeps copies of records on several machines. If the primary server fails, a replica can take over, although recent unreplicated writes may be lost.

sources.title: replication b
sources.text: A database backup is a periodic snapshot stored offline. Restoring a large snapshot can take hours and requires a tested recovery procedure.

sources.title: vaccine a
sources.text: Vaccination exposes the immune system to a harmless antigen. Memory cells then enable a faster response when the actual pathogen is encountered later.

sources.title: vaccine b
sources.text: Antibiotics inhibit bacterial growth or kill bacteria. They do not directly treat viral infections, and unnecessary prescribing promotes resistance.

sources.title: island a
sources.text: Dark roofs and roads absorb solar energy and release heat after sunset. Sparse vegetation and these surfaces make densely built districts warmer than nearby rural areas.

sources.title: island b
sources.text: Urban air pollution includes particulate matter from traffic. Exposure varies with wind direction, vehicle emissions and proximity to major roads.

sources.title: resistance a
sources.text: Repeated exposure to an antibiotic selects bacteria carrying resistance genes. Susceptible cells die while resistant survivors reproduce and spread their traits.

sources.title: resistance b
sources.text: Bacteria can ferment sugars without oxygen. The resulting acids are useful in food production, including yogurt and some preserved vegetables.

sources.title: glacier a
sources.text: Glaciers store snowfall as compressed ice over many years. When summer melting exceeds winter accumulation, a glacier loses mass and its terminus often retreats.

sources.title: glacier b
sources.text: Sea ice forms when ocean water freezes. Its seasonal extent changes rapidly, and unlike land ice its melting has little direct effect on sea level.

sources.title: cache a
sources.text: A cache stores frequently requested results near the client to avoid repeating expensive work. Stale entries must be invalidated when the underlying data changes.

sources.title: cache b
sources.text: A message queue buffers work for background workers. Acknowledgments and retries help tasks survive temporary worker failures.

sources.title: pollination a
sources.text: Bees carry pollen between flowers as they forage for nectar. This transfer enables fertilization and supports seed production in many flowering crops.

sources.title: pollination b
sources.text: Wind pollination releases large quantities of light pollen into the air. Grasses often rely on this mechanism rather than attracting animal visitors.
